name: r12_frame_with_a_thinner_profile
why: A welded frame whose PROFILE is changed: the tube goes from 80 to 60. The mitre at the corners is redone with different faces, and if a corner does not close two bars merge into a single body or one is left detached. Four bars must stay four.
_why_it_is_not_the_length: Entry F8 here asked for «frame 1000x800, 1000 -> 1400». IT CANNOT BE EXPRESSED TODAY: the path of a frame is a `3DProfileFeature`, and the state does not publish its dimensions -- `set_dimension` has nothing to name. The only dimensions the state exposes are those of the tube PROFILE (D1 = 80, D2 = 6, D3 = 5), and that is the one changed here. Found out by measuring, after two cases had been misclassified by guessing the name.
_why_the_dimension_names_no_sketch: D1 is the side of the profile, and the sketch that holds it came from the profile file of the library, whose names stay in the language the file was made in: the dimension is asked for by its name alone (the frame has no other D1), so the case does not depend on the language of SOLIDWORKS.
intent_why: the path of the frame does not change: four bars remain laid out as before, and the centroid of a symmetric frame stays where it is. If a corner is lost, the symmetry goes and it shows.

after.tolerance_why: the centroid of a symmetric frame is at the centre and stays there: half a millimetre on a one-metre part is much less than it would move if a corner were lost
